# Complete application authentication examples

Choose oidc + web for Google/GitHub, password/ for a username/password laboratory,
or introspection/ for an existing verifier. See ../../references/application-auth.md.
Configure public origin/Client IDs in site-config.mjs. Secret values remain in Site
Settings. OAuth front/back use the same resolver. Build in oidc with npm ci,
npm test, npm run build; upload only web/ and oidc/dist/function/.
Password schema must be planned against the actual database; never apply it blindly
on an existing app. Both examples filter business rows by verified app identity.
The OAuth notes form keeps the original command and idempotency key after a
network failure, timeout, or server failure. A definite first-attempt 4xx rejection (except
408) restores editing and preserves the entered text; the next submission uses
a new key. Once an attempt has an unknown outcome, later rejections retain that
original key because they cannot rule out an earlier commit. A failed refresh after a successful write never replays the write.

## Local HTTPS

Use Node 22.12+ and a certificate/key valid for localhost, stored outside upload roots. Reuse a suitable existing pair or the environment's existing certificate tool. The OpenSSL example below is optional: first check `openssl version` and that `openssl req -help` supports `-addext`.

```sh
mkdir -p .local-tls
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -keyout .local-tls/key.pem -out .local-tls/cert.pem -subj /CN=localhost -addext 'subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1'
node dev/server.mjs --mode password --port 8443 --cert .local-tls/cert.pem --key .local-tls/key.pem
```

If OpenSSL is missing or lacks that option, pass a pair generated by an available certificate tool to the same Node command. If no pair can be supplied, continue the bundled protocol tests (`node --test password/test/check.mjs`, or `npm ci` and `npm test` in `oidc/`) and leave local HTTPS browser checks pending. An already authorized HTTPS deployment can supply the browser test environment; missing local tools do not authorize publication. Preserve Secure cookies and TLS checks.

Use a trusted local certificate or accept this disposable certificate in the test
browser. Never weaken production Cookie or TLS checks. The server binds loopback
only and exits on a port conflict, preserving existing processes. Stop it and wait
for exit before restarting. GET /__local_health identifies the selected mode.
OAuth mode uses synthetic configuration and blocks provider traffic; it checks
rendering/CSRF and does not prove external OAuth. Password mode keeps data in memory.
The fake database is for local behavior tests, not Provider concurrency evidence.
Neither mode accesses cloud data or loads production credentials.

For real deployment use the formal HTTPS host and runtime acceptance checklist.
